_readme: Turns a real model is asked to READ, once a guard has let them through.
The extraction contract is literal: values may only hold what the member
actually said, a choice must be one of the printed options spelled exactly,
and anything unclear is left out rather than guessed. Half of these scenarios
test that the model records what is there; the other half test that it records
nothing when there is nothing to record, which is the harder half and the one
that costs a member a wrong answer in their file when it goes wrong.
awaiting     the slot the caller just asked for, or ""
last_agent   what the caller said, verbatim enough for context
expect       slot -> value that MUST be recorded, spelled exactly
expect_absent slots that must NOT be recorded from this turn
expect_corrections  slot -> value that must arrive as a correction
expect_declines     true when the member refused the question
Every field is optional but 'member'. Assert only what the scenario is about.

scenarios.last_agent: Have you had a chance to review any of the program resources — the action plans, articles, videos or websites?
scenarios.member: Yes, I had a look at a few of the articles.

scenarios.last_agent: How helpful were they in making at least one lifestyle change? Extremely helpful; somewhat helpful; not very helpful; definitely not helpful.
scenarios.member: Somewhat, I'd say. They gave me a couple of ideas.
scenarios.why: The option value, not the member's wording, is what may be recorded.

scenarios.last_agent: How would you rate your experience with the program overall? Extremely helpful; somewhat helpful; not very helpful; definitely not helpful.
scenarios.member: Oh, it was alright I suppose. Can't complain.
scenarios.why: 'Alright' is nearest to somewhat_helpful and must still not be recorded. A rating the member did not give is worse than no rating.

scenarios.last_agent: How would you rate your experience with the program overall? Extremely helpful; somewhat helpful; not very helpful; definitely not helpful.
scenarios.member: Somewhere in the middle, I'd say. Mustn't grumble.
scenarios.why: The nearest option is somewhat_helpful and it is still a guess. A wrong rating is worse than a gap, because a gap is reported as one.

scenarios.last_agent: How would you rate your experience with the program overall? Extremely helpful; somewhat helpful; not very helpful; definitely not helpful.
scenarios.member: Extremely helpful. Genuinely, it changed how I eat.
scenarios.why: The other side of the scenario above — restraint must not become deafness.

scenarios.last_agent: What changes or additions would you like to see that would improve the program? No or none is a perfectly good answer.
scenarios.member: No, nothing I can think of.
scenarios.why: On the two feedback questions this IS the answer, not a refusal. Getting it wrong reports a member who answered as one who declined.

scenarios.last_agent: What changes or additions would you like to see that would improve the program?
scenarios.member: I'd rather not get into all that, if it's all the same to you.
scenarios.why: The mirror of the scenario above. These two are one word apart in the transcript and a survey apart in the result.

scenarios.last_agent: Have you had a chance to review any of the program resources?
scenarios.member: Yes I did, and they were extremely helpful actually — I've started walking every morning because of them.
scenarios.why: A member answering ahead is being helpful. The whole point of offering the model the questionnaire rather than one slot.

scenarios.last_agent: What changes or additions would you like to see that would improve the program?
scenarios.member: Actually, hang on — I said I'd looked at the resources, but I never did get round to opening any of them.
scenarios.why: A correction four questions later. It should arrive as a correction, not as a fresh value, and it re-opens question 1b.

scenarios.last_agent: Would you recommend the program to people you know?
scenarios.member: I honestly couldn't tell you. I don't really know anyone who'd need it.
scenarios.why: The prompt says not knowing is not a refusal. It is an unclear answer, which is retried rather than settled.

scenarios.last_agent: May I speak to Margaret Ellison?
scenarios.member: There's no Margaret here. You've got the wrong number, love.
scenarios.why: The difference between a work item worth retrying tomorrow and a number that should never be dialled for this member again.

scenarios.last_agent: May I speak to Margaret Ellison?
scenarios.member: She's my mother — she's having a nap just now. Can I take a message?
scenarios.why: Right household, wrong person. Retryable, unlike the scenario above.

scenarios.last_agent: Would you recommend the program to people you know?
scenarios.member: Yes I would. Who is it you said you were calling from again?
scenarios.why: Answered and asked something back. The answer must still land, and the question should surface as a secondary intent.
